issue_context.title: slerp functions for directions (Vec2 and Vec3)
issue_context.body:
## What problem does this solve or what need does it fill?

Linear interpolation is unsuited for transitioning of directions.

## What solution would you like?

I would like a spherical interpolation function (slerp) for Vec2 and Vec3 directions.

## Additional context

This is a common feature in existing game engines:
https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_vector3.html#class-vector3-method-slerp
https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Vector3.Slerp.html
comments: [Vec2 and Vec3 is part of glam crate](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/11f0a2dcdeb86651fdb6cdaf2c83ffd01df93149/crates/bevy_math/src/common_traits.rs#L1), this problem should be solved there, futhermore there is already [long living issue](https://github.com/bitshifter/glam-rs/issues/377)

@bugsweeper You're right that the vector types are owned by glam, but on the other hand, we could easily implement `slerp` functions for the `Dir2`/`Dir3` types that we *do* own, and I think those would be quite useful.

review_comments: This implementation should probably just use `Quat::from_rotation_arc` on the underlying vectors instead of trying to do all the logic itself.

I changed to Quat calculation, and it is less precise
```
let quat = Quat::IDENTITY.slerp(
    Quat::from_rotation_arc(self.0, rhs.0),
    s,
);
Dir3(quat.mul_vec3(self.0))
```
gives error:
```
assert_relative_eq!(Dir3::X.slerp(Dir3::Z, 1.0 / 3.0), Dir3::from_xyz(0.75f32.sqrt(), 0.0, 0.5).unwrap())

    left  = Dir3(Vec3(0.86602515, 0.0, 0.49999994))
    right = Dir3(Vec3(0.8660254, 0.0, 0.5))
```

I guess I don't really see that as a big problem; I'd still rather use `Quat::from_rotation_arc` than maintain additional logic which is essentially the same (and the degree of precision used in the test can be changed).
